updates.reason: E132 at 100 seeds: trimming 16 px from 2.0 to 1.5 epochs cost -0.17 pp for -3.1% time (~0.055-0.075 pp per 1%). The prediction was <=0.017 pp per 1%, and the result sits at or above the 0.05 yardstick. Caveat from the review: E132 rescaled LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence to the shorter total, so it also changed the schedule of every later phase. The clean version moves to the frontier node.

The prediction that 16 px samples are the cheapest to remove failed at 100 seeds (E132). Removing early samples costs about as much per 1% of time as removing 32 px samples (E128). Only the mechanism's confounded test exists; a clean test is registered under the new frontier node.

updates.statement: (Descriptive only, mechanism refuted) Early-phase response is asymmetric. Adding early updates or samples gains nothing (E121 +0.004 pp, E114 +0.02 pp at 100 seeds). Removing them costs at or above the yardstick: E134 early bs 2048 -0.30 pp (~0.2 pp per 1%), E132 16 px trim -0.17 pp, E093 whitening-bias freeze at 3% -0.44 pp, E032 no bridge -0.68 pp. The registered falsifiable predictions (early bs 2048 null; 16 px trim well under 0.05 pp per 1%) both failed. The 'threshold on update count, not samples' claim fails because removing samples also hurt (E132). Superseded by the frontier Lvl1, which explains the same pattern without a phase-specific mechanism.
updates.reason: Both of H8's falsifiable predictions were refuted at 100 seeds (E134, E132). The remaining content is a description of the data, and the new frontier Lvl1 covers it better.

E134 at 100 seeds: -0.30 pp for -1.3% time (~0.2 pp per 1%), far above the <=0.03 pp predicted. Confounds: the whitening-bias detach stayed sample-indexed, so the 64x-LR bias got ~25% fewer steps (E093 shows it is fragile), and the SGD groups were kilostep-rescaled. The batch lever is closed as a time lever either way, since even a clean version would need to lose <0.07 pp.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size, read through critical batch size. Early (16/24 px): B_crit lies between 1536 and 2048. Going smaller gains nothing (E121, bs 1024: +0.004 pp at 100 seeds); going larger costs a lot (E134, bs 2048 with step-fixed warmup: -0.30 pp; confounded by fewer whitening-bias steps and the SGD rescale). Late (28/32 px): bs 1024 is a real purchase. E126 at 100 seeds shows bs 1536 costs -0.18 pp for -2.1%, ~0.085 pp per 1%, which confirms the direction of E084 (the E121 note calling E084 'likely noise' was wrong about direction). Open puzzle: the late B_crit looks smaller than the early one, the reverse of gradient-noise-scale theory (1812.06162). E126's confounds (EMA-window samples, SGD rescale, Muon path length) may produce this; H11.2.2 decides. Batch size is closed as a time lever in both phases.
updates.reason: Folds in E134 and restates the node in critical-batch terms, as the review asked. Also corrects the E121 note: E126 confirmed E084's direction at large seed.

E133 (80% freeze, 200 trajectories): -0.10 pp vs E116 for -1.7% time. The 85->80 marginal rate is ~0.06 ± ~0.015 pp per 1%, at the pre-registered >0.06 cut-off and ~1 SE above the 0.044 re-spend rate. The 75% arm was gated on <=0.04 and was not run. Practical decision: the freeze stays at 85%. Per the review, the rejection is partly a policy decision: E133's population of 0.75106 misses the 0.7513 floor by ~1.3 SE. This is not a clean accuracy refutation.

updates.statement: Late layer freezing is a real rate lever with a small, real accuracy cost. Stem + group 1 frozen from 85% of samples: -4.5% time, -0.09 pp (E118, 198 trajectories), banked (E119). From 92%: -2.5%, -0.02 pp (E120). From 80%: a further -1.7% for -0.10 pp (E133), a marginal ~0.06 pp per 1%, so 85% is at or near the optimum. Closed: group-2 freeze (E125, ~0.055 pp per 1%), FreezeOut LR anneal (E129, +0.002), and caching frozen-layer activations (search 2508.15033: fails under flip/translate augmentation). Open: BN eval mode in the frozen window (H2.20.6, FreezeOut's own design per search 1706.04983) and progressive freeze (very low prior).
updates.reason: Adds E133 and the search findings (FreezeOut does use BN eval mode; activation caching is incompatible with augmentation).

Search: putting frozen layers in inference mode and skipping their mean/variance computation is FreezeOut's original design (1706.04983), not an add-on. The byte saving falls on the largest 31x31x128 activations, and the search's PCIe estimate says energy and byte levers transfer to the 300 W judge. One of the few zero-accuracy-risk time levers left.
Search (2508.15033) closes the natural activation-caching extension. Progressive freeze still has only tiny-CNN evidence, and the FreezeOut anneal (E129) found no abruptness cost to recover.

E131 at 100 seeds: translate 4 in the 28/32 px phases cost -0.56 pp vs E116. The comparison baseline is mismatched: E131 was built on E100, which sits ~+0.09 pp above E116, so the true effect is ~-0.65 pp. Strongly refuted either way.

updates.statement: (Upward direction only) Stronger augmentation under Muon hurts: translate 4 cost ~-0.6 pp (E131), duplicated draws ~-0.9 pp (E124), and jitter hurt under SGD (E008). This refutes only the 'more augmentation' half. The weaker direction is a separate node (weaker augmentation under H12).
updates.reason: E131 refutes the upward direction. The review notes that a steep downward slope at translate 2 leaves the optimum possibly below 2, so the weaker direction is split out instead of closing augmentation strength.

updates.statement: Under Muon, data composition and augmentation strength are zero-time accuracy sources, and the current setting may sit above the short-budget optimum. Evidence: the accuracy response to augmentation and coverage is steep. Translate 4 cost ~-0.6 pp (E131) and halving unique 32 px coverage ~-0.9 pp (E124), both at 100 seeds. Class balance is null (E112). Augmentation was closed after testing only the upward direction. The recipe is under-trained (~1 pp per 32 px epoch, E128), which favors weaker augmentation, especially in the late 28/32 px phases. Live: translate 1/0 and flip removal late (weaker augmentation node).
updates.reason: E131/E124 show a steep response to augmentation. The review identifies the untested weaker direction as the best-motivated zero-time accuracy source, so the prior rises.

updates.statement: Depth cuts are FLOP-proportional time levers but do not beat the yardstick. 2/3/3: -0.29 pp for -7.0% (~0.04 pp per 1%, E127). Re-spent at 32 px at the upward rate (~0.044 pp per 1%, E128 +0.25 arm), it roughly breaks even, and additivity is untested. 3/3/2: -0.48 pp for -6.3% (~0.08 pp per 1%, E130). Closed.
updates.reason: E130 refutes the 3/3/2 arm at 100 seeds. The 2/3/3 arm trades at the re-spend rate, so there is no net gain.
E130 was exactly this run: -0.48 pp at 100 seeds for -6.3%, beyond the >=0.30 pp closing bar.

updates.statement: Levers that trade below the re-spend rate can be combined with 32 px re-spend for a net time gain at constant population mean. Corrected rates: re-spend (upward) ~0.044 pp per 1% (E128 +0.25 arm), pure cut ~0.054. After E130-E134 the only measured lever below 0.044 is the already-banked 85% freeze. 2/3/3 (~0.041) breaks even. On hold until at least two new levers are measured below ~0.04 pp per 1%.
updates.reason: The review points out that no candidate levers remain: the 80% freeze, 3/3/2, early bs 2048 and the 16 px trim all came in at or above 0.054.

Its preconditions failed: every lever it planned to combine (75/80% freeze E133, 3/3/2 E130, early bs 2048 E134, 16 px trim E132) measured at or above ~0.055 pp per 1%. The only borderline lever left is 2/3/3 at 0.041 against a 0.044 re-spend rate, which nets ~0.

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Cost is FLOP-proportional for group-3 width (E117), depth (E123/E127/E130) and the late freeze. It is not FLOP-proportional for narrow group-2 widths (E080) or for pool and activation ops (E052, E023). FreezeOut's measured speedup exceeded its FLOP estimate by 1.3x (search), weak support for a byte term. Tip: E116/E119 code, ~4.26 s, population mean 0.7521. Yardstick (E128): pure cut ~0.054 pp per 1%, re-spend ~0.044 pp per 1%. Measured lever rates in pp per 1%: 85% freeze ~0.02 (banked); 85->80% ~0.06; 2/3/3 ~0.04; 3/3/2 ~0.08; group-2 freeze ~0.055; 16 px trim ~0.055-0.075; early bs 2048 ~0.2; late bs 1536 ~0.085. Live levers (untested): BN-eval in the frozen window (H2.20.6), group-3 width 512 (H2.19.2), a structural redesign of the 31x31 stage (earlier downsample or group-1 width; frontier node), lookahead removal (H9.2.2), activation under Muon (re-screen node), Muon-C (low). Closed: CUDA graphs, Inductor tuning, cuDNN settings, prepare, group-2 width, depth cuts, batch-size levers in every phase, freeze earlier than 85%, the 28 px substitution, phase trims, the group-2 freeze, the freeze anneal.
updates.reason: Prunes the live list after E130-E134, per the review, and adds the corrected up/down yardstick rates.

updates.statement: The local yardstick, measured on the tip (E128, 100 seeds per arm): 32 px phase -0.25 / +0.25 epoch gave -0.25 / +0.24 pp, i.e. ~1 pp per 32 px epoch. As rates: pure cut ~0.054 pp per 1% of time, re-spend ~0.044 pp per 1%. A low-res trim has now been measured at large seed: 16 px 2->1.5 epochs cost -0.17 pp for -3.1% (E132), no better than the 32 px rate. Equal-time low-res/high-res reshuffles are null (E114). Every phase trim now trades at or above the yardstick.
updates.reason: The statement was stale: it said low-res trims had never been measured at large seed, but E132 has measured one. The single yardstick is split into separate pure-cut and re-spend rates.

updates.statement: (Weakened) Late full-resolution training binds accuracy. What holds: fresh 32 px images matter (E124, ~-0.9 pp from duplicates), late updates matter on the downside (E126, -0.18 pp; confounded by EMA-window samples, SGD rescale and Muon path length), and 32 px epochs give ±1 pp per epoch (E128). What is NOT shown: that late training is special. Early decrements cost as much or more (E134 -0.30, E132 -0.17), and no late increment has been tested at large seed. Late Muon lr (E100/E110/E111) and an equal-time 24/32 swap (E114) are null. Distinguishing test: a late increment (H2.11.5) after the E126 confound ablation (H11.2.2). If late increments also saturate, H11 collapses into the frontier Lvl1.
updates.reason: The review shows the decrement evidence is not late-specific. E134/E132 cost as much as the late decrements. Confidence is lowered.

The 'late steps worth more than early steps' contrast rests on a late decrement (E126) against an early increment (E121). Early decrements (E134 -0.30) hurt even more, so placement-specificity is not established until a late increment and the E126 confound ablation (H11.2.2) are run.
The E121 100-seed replicate (the large-seed paired replicate this node asked for) gave +0.004 pp, within the predicted <=+0.03. E104's +0.12 was one-process noise.

updates.statement: (Gated) A late increment: bs 768 in the last ~1 epoch of the 32 px phase. Run only after H11.2.2 shows that E126's loss came from update count. Step 1, untimed: profile bs 768 at 32 px (static, warmed) and project total time. Step 2: 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline (sample-indexed; final-EMA/lookahead pinned to the last 8 steps; SGD groups kilostep-scaled; Muon unchanged). Prediction (H11): gain >=+0.08 pp at <=+2.5% time, i.e. >=0.05 pp per 1%, beating the 0.044 re-spend rate. Prediction (frontier Lvl1): gain <=0.044 pp per 1%. If the gain is <=0.03 pp, increments saturate late too.
updates.reason: Gated behind the confound ablation per the review. It is also now the distinguishing test between H11 and the new frontier Lvl1.

Review argument: every Muon matrix has out < in (filters [Cout, 9*Cin], head [100, 576]). A full-row-rank semi-orthogonal update UV^T already has unit-norm rows, so NorMuon's row normalization would only correct NS imprecision. E033 (NS 4, better orthogonalization) gained nothing. The evidence is LM-only.
Parent retired on the row-norm argument; no run needed.

updates.statement: Muon-C: orthogonalizing each frequency block of the 3x3-DFT of the kernel momentum gives better-conditioned conv updates. Corrected evidence (search 2609.09676): the classification gains (+0.26 to +0.60 pp over unfolded Muon) were measured on ImageNet-100 at 100 epochs, not on short budgets. The short-budget claim comes from CIFAR-10 flow-matching FID. Measured optimizer overhead is ~2x unfolded Muon's (1.36x vs 1.18x of Adam's step), which projects to ~+4-5% time if applied only in the 16/24 px phases. Local evidence against the mechanism: better conditioning (NS 4, E033) bought nothing at this budget. Very low prior.
updates.reason: The search corrects the framing (long-budget gains, ~2x overhead). The review notes E033 is direct evidence that conditioning does not bind here.
Measured overhead (search) projects ~+4-5% time in the low-res phases, so the <=+3% gate in step 1 will likely fail. Keep only as an untimed overhead check.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Closed: momentum (on 3-seed evidence; re-screen node), NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers, Muon lr in every phase (E105, E107, E110, E111), freeze LR anneal (E129), NorMuon (retired on the row-norm argument). The head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are kept, but a population-level audit is pending (H13.1.1). Muon-C is very low prior: its gains are long-budget, overhead ~2x, and E033 shows conditioning does not bind. Schedule shape (H7.4) is very low prior.
updates.reason: Adds the search corrections on Muon-C, retires NorMuon, and flags that momentum was closed on 3-seed evidence.
Search: hiverge and airbench SOTAs use plain linear decay. The one claimed vision WSD result (2601.09000) did not hold up on fetch: CIFAR-10 tiny CNN only, 'comparable'.
No verified vision support for WSD at short budgets (search).

updates.statement: Acceptance rule, pre-registered and not adjusted per candidate. (1) Official safety: population mean mu >= 0.7513 on >=100 trajectories, i.e. >=3 sd of the 40-seed mean above 0.75. This is a hard policy floor; candidates that miss it by <2 SE (E133: 0.75106, ~1.3 SE short) are reported as policy rejections, not accuracy refutations. (2) Local gate: at most 3 scored attempts per code, stopping at the first row >=0.753. Every scored rerun of the same code counts toward the budget, including tip reruns attached to other experiments. E116 code already has 7 rows, which lifts the pass chance from ~61% to ~89% and voids the intended budget. (3) Every banked time is reported with Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and its observed pass count (E116 code: ~27% per attempt, 2/7). (4) Precondition before any final submission: submissions/arena must hold the banked E116 code, not E133's (E133 is marked feasible/improved in results.tsv and could be picked by a best-feasible-row selection). Margin policy: a cut may lower mu only down to 0.7513, and only at <=0.054 pp per 1% or funded at the 0.044 re-spend rate.
updates.reason: Review: the attempt budget is being bypassed by tip reruns, E133 is a policy rejection rather than a refutation, and there is a risk of the wrong arena code being selected.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed and free, and a precondition for every later decision. Still to do: (1) git-diff E077-E084 against their stated base; (2) resolve the E092/E093 and E103/E105 base mismatches; (3) E123's idea says it reruns E090, but its 4.258 s matches E116; E124's idea says base E100 but it was compared with E116. (4) New mismatches: E124 and E131 were built on E100 (no freeze, ~+0.09 pp above E116) but compared with the E116 vector, so their true deltas are ~-0.91 and ~-0.65 pp. Verdicts are unchanged, but 0.05-0.09 pp offsets now matter. Recompute every large-seed delta against the baseline of its actual base code. From now on, 'source hash = stated base, and the comparison baseline is from the same base' is a hard precondition logged in every idea.
updates.reason: Review found additional baseline mismatches (E124, E131) at a precision where they matter.

Search: FreezeOut's measured speedup exceeded its FLOP estimate by 1.3x under linear scheduling, weak outside support for a byte term. Still inconclusive locally. Per the review, it matters only if it points to a lever; the structural-redesign node now tests the lever directly.
Deprioritized: reconciling the model cannot by itself produce a speedup. Run only alongside the structural-redesign profile, to explain its result.
Deprioritized per the review: it is an explanatory tool, not a lever. Use it after the fact to interpret structural profiles.
Deprioritized; free analysis only, no runs.
Moved, ungated, to the new structural-redesign node under the frontier Lvl1. The review recommends profiling directly instead of waiting on the cost model.

Search supports the premise: the 300 W PCIe card sustains ~90% of SXM4 throughput and sits deeper in the energy-bound regime, so energy and byte levers should transfer at least proportionally. Still a tie-breaker only.

Search: hiverge's tuned Muon CIFAR-10 SOTA uses no EMA or lookahead at all, an outside prior that the averaging pieces may be removable. The 100-seed removal tests (H9.2.2/H9.2.3) are cheap and decisive and should be run next.

Review: the removal ablations (H13.1.1, H9.2.2, H9.2.3) are the cheapest zero-time margin sources left, and none has been run at 100 seeds. hiverge (search) uses no averaging and LS 0.09, which raises the chance that some tip component is null.
E132 shows 16 px samples carry accuracy at about the yardstick rate, so swapping 16 px for less informative 12 px is unlikely to trade well.

updates.statement: On the E116 base, set group-3 width to 512 (head [100, 512], Muon stacks re-batched, all freeze x renorm variants warmed). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Bar at the pure-cut rate (0.054 pp per 1%): -5.2% x 0.054 ≈ 0.28 pp. Prediction: loss <=0.18 pp. If the loss is >=0.28 pp, the cut trades no better than a 32 px trim and group-3 width closes. Low prior: futurebiohackers chose 576 because late width buys CIFAR-100 accuracy (E005), and 3/3/2 (also a group-3 capacity cut) traded at ~0.08 (E130).
updates.reason: Updates the bar to the corrected pure-cut rate and adds E130 as evidence against group-3 capacity cuts.

new.statement: The tip sits on an equalized-marginal-rate frontier. Greedy banking pushed each schedule, batch, freeze and depth lever to roughly the same exchange rate, so every remaining trade of existing phases, freeze points or batch sizes costs ~0.044-0.06 pp per 1% of time (E128 0.054/0.044, E132 0.055-0.075, E125 0.055, E133 0.06, E127 0.04). Increments saturate (E121, E114). Consequence: further gains need either new zero-time accuracy (large-seed re-screens, removal ablations, weaker augmentation) or a structural change that moves the frontier. Falsifiable: a clean trim that is not a schedule-rescale artifact still costs >=0.044 pp per 1%, and a late increment buys <=0.044 pp per 1%.

The ~0.05 pp per 1% cost of phase trims reflects the marginal value of the removed training itself, not side effects of rescaling the LR/floor/renorm schedule or of shortening the whitening-bias window (the E132/E134 confounds).

Clean 16 px trim on E116 code: drop only the first 0.5 epoch of 16 px. Keep the absolute sample positions of everything after it (LR warmup end, decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, whitening-bias detach, 85% freeze, 28/32 px switches), i.e. start the schedule 0.5 epoch in, with warmup kept in steps. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline, same-base comparison. Prediction (frontier): loss >=0.12 pp for ~-3% (>=0.04 pp per 1%). If the loss is <=0.05 pp, E132's cost was a rescale artifact; reopen the 16 px trim as a lever and mark H8.3 as a confounded refutation.

A structural redesign of the high-resolution 31x31x128 stage (stem + group 1) can move the frontier. That stage carries ~31% of backward time at 32 px (E122: 3.75 of 12.0 ms), plus its BN/GELU bytes on the largest activations, while group 1's third conv cost only ~0.04 pp per 1% to remove (E127). Cheaper early spatial processing trades capacity where it is least valuable. Risk: early high-resolution features were fragile (E093, E032).

Untimed profile on E116 code (all shapes x freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variants warmed) of three variants: (a) group 1's max-pool moved from after conv3 to after conv1, so conv2/conv3 run at 15x15; (b) group-1 width 96; (c) both. Project total time over the E116 schedule. Prediction: at least one variant projects >=8% saving. Score at 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline only those that do, with the bar at <=0.044 pp per 1% (fundable by 32 px re-spend). If none projects >=8%, close structural early-stage changes without accuracy runs.

Zero-time knobs closed on single 3-seed runs before the large-seed instrument existed (E113) hide >=0.1 pp of population accuracy. Those runs had a two-arm SE of ~0.2 pp, so effects up to ~±0.3 pp were never excluded: LS (E037, E009), Muon momentum (E030, E027), warmup (E051, E059), the Muon floor (E057), the whitening-bias window (E061), the activation (E003, SGD only). The 100-seed instrument resolves ~0.07 pp at 2 SE, and +0.1 pp buys ~2% time through a 32 px trim at 0.054 pp per 1%.

Label smoothing 0.3 was tuned under SGD at 8.5 epochs. Under Muon on the shorter tip it may be over-regularized: tuned Muon CIFAR recipes use LS 0.09 (hiverge, search), and every augmentation increase hurt strongly (E131, E124), consistent with an under-fit regime.

On E116 code, two untimed arms of 100 seeds each vs the pooled E116 baseline: LS 0.2 and LS 0.25 (a loss constant, nothing recompiles). Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp. If both are within ±0.05 pp, LS is closed at population level.

Optimizer scalars closed on 3-seed evidence may hide margin: Muon momentum (only 0.5/0.6/0.85 tested, 3 seeds each; hiverge uses 0.655), the 64x LR multiplier on the SGD-trained BN biases, and BN momentum. Each is a 0-d tensor or host constant, so arms cost nothing in time.

On E116 code, untimed arms of 100 seeds each vs the pooled E116 baseline: Muon momentum 0.5 and 0.7; BN-bias SGD multiplier 32x and 96x. Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp. If all four are within ±0.05 pp, optimizer scalars are closed at population level. Expect momentum 0.7 to be the riskiest arm, given E027's -1.18 pp at 0.85.

GELU->SiLU was rejected under SGD on one 3-seed run (E003: -2.2% time, -0.61 pp). Under Muon the accuracy cost of the activation has never been measured. At the 0.054 pp per 1% pure-cut rate, a -2.2% saving breaks even at <=0.12 pp loss.

Untimed per-step profile of the E116 tip with SiLU (and ReLU) in place of GELU, all variants warmed. Only if the projected saving is >=2%, run 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: loss <=0.10 pp, i.e. <=0.05 pp per 1%. If the saving is <1.5% or the loss is >=0.15 pp, the activation is closed under Muon.

Weaker augmentation in the late phases. The accuracy response to more augmentation is steep (translate 4 -0.6 pp, E131), so translate 2 may itself be above the short-budget optimum. Under-training (~1 pp per 32 px epoch) favors less late regularization. Flip remains the safest augmentation to keep.

On E116 code, in the 28/32 px phases only, run untimed arms of 100 seeds each vs the pooled E116 baseline (same base): translate 1 and translate 0 (flip kept), with the pad width as a host-side constant per phase and both variants warmed. Time within ±0.5%. Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp. If translate 1 is within ±0.05 pp and translate 0 loses, translate 2 is at the optimum and augmentation strength closes in both directions.

On E116 code, disable the alternating flip in the last 32 px epoch only (translate 2 kept; host-side flag, nothing recompiles). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: gain >=+0.06 pp, since late training on the test distribution helps under-fit models. If the loss is >=0.05 pp, late flip is still useful regularization.

Revision after E125–E134. Every lever tried since E125 traded at or worse than the measured yardstick (pure cut ~0.054 pp per 1% of time; re-spending time at 32 px buys back ~0.044). I updated the tree to match:

**Closed or downgraded**
- **Refuted:**
  - H8.3.1 and H8.3: the 16 px trim cost -0.17 pp at 100 seeds (E132). That test is confounded by the schedule rescale, so a clean version is registered.
  - H2.11.7: early bs 2048 cost -0.30 pp (E134).
  - H12.3.1 and H12.3: translate 4 cost about -0.6 pp (E131).
  - H2.18 and H2.18.4: 3/3/2 cost -0.48 pp (E130).
- **H8:** its falsifiable predictions both failed, so it is now marked refuted and kept only as a description: adding early training gains nothing, removing it costs.
- **H2.20.2 (80% freeze):** inconclusive. The marginal rate is ~0.06 pp per 1%, about 1 SE above the 0.044 re-spend rate, so the freeze stays at 85%. The E133 rejection is recorded as a policy decision, not an accuracy refutation.
- **H2.23.1** is retired because every lever it planned to combine failed, and H2.23 is on hold.
- **H11 and H11.2** are lowered: losses from removing training are not specific to late phases (E134 and E132 cost as much as or more than E126). H2.11.5 now waits on the E126 confound ablation (H11.2.2).
- **H7.5 (NorMuon)** is retired on the row-norm argument.
- **H7.6 (Muon-C)** is corrected per the search: its gains were measured at long budgets, its overhead is ~2x, and E033 shows better-conditioned updates don't bind here.
- **H2.21.4** is moved, ungated, to a new structural node.

**Restated nodes**
- **H2:** the live-lever list is pruned, and the yardstick is split into the 0.054 pure-cut and 0.044 re-spend rates.
- **H2.11:** restated in critical-batch-size terms.
- **H2.10:** now includes E132.
- **H4.9:** every scored rerun of the same code counts toward the 3-attempt budget, the floor is a hard policy rule, and submissions/arena must hold E116 code before final submission.
- **H4.2.4:** E124 and E131 were compared against the wrong baseline (E116 instead of their E100 base), so their true deltas are about 0.09 pp worse.
- **Search findings added:** support for FreezeOut's BN-eval-while-frozen design (H2.20.6), for the judge-transfer premise (H2.4.3), and for removing averaging, since hiverge uses none (H9, H13).
